title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Physical context: this is a handwritten sheet on the verso of a typescript page of SGA 7 Exp. IX (Grothendieck's 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'). The typed text shows through, and the neighbouring archive pages are typed SGA 7 IX pp. 50-51. The handwriting belongs to the 1975-76 work on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex.

Goal stated in the first lines: 'let us try to determine the invariants of φ_*', an endomorphism of a complete differential PD bialgebra, apparently of 'Witt' type. This looks like a tower or filtered object (φ_0, φ_1, ..., φ_n) built over a base S_k. Each layer φ_n is φ_0-semilinear.

Invariant 1: a bialgebra endomorphism φ_0 of B_k. It is given by elements τ_i = φ_0(T^i) in S_k, i ≥ 1, subject to τ_i τ_j = c_{ij} τ_{i+j}. With c_{ij} presumably the binomial coefficient C(i+j, i), this says (τ_i) is a divided-power sequence, i.e. a 'PD point'. So φ_0 amounts to a morphism out of a polynomial / divided-power Hopf algebra, via the standard duality k[T] ↔ Γ(T).

Invariant 2: φ_1, a φ_0-semilinear endomorphism of S_k{X_0}[dX_0]. This is the PD de Rham complex in one variable over S_k: divided-power polynomials in X_0 with the odd generator dX_0, viewed as a differential algebra. It must be compatible with the augmentation.

Proposition (one-variable classification). Let φ_0 : S → S' be a ring map. Augmented differential-ring homomorphisms φ_1 : A_S = S{X_0}[dX_0] → A_{S'} lying over φ_0 correspond canonically to systems ξ_i ∈ A_{S'}^+, where:
- ξ_i = A_i + B_i dX_0, with A_i ∈ S'{X_0}^+ and B_i ∈ S'{X_0};
- A_i = A_1^{[i]};
- φ_1(X_0^{[i]}) = ξ_i and φ_1(dX_0) = dξ_1.

Compatibility conditions:
- φ_1 respects the grading iff B_i = 0 for all i.
- φ_1 respects divided powers iff B_i = A_1^{[i-1]} B_1 for i ≥ 2. This is the formula (a + bε)^{[i]} = a^{[i]} + a^{[i-1]} bε for ε odd with ε² = 0.

So Grothendieck deliberately allows morphisms that do NOT preserve the de Rham degree: degree 0 may map into degree 0 ⊕ degree 1. This is the 'superalgebra' viewpoint, in which the de Rham complex is the ring of functions on an odd tangent bundle.

The list of conditions the ξ_i must satisfy ('satisfaisant à : ...') is left blank. The remaining conditions are the differential compatibility dξ_i = ξ_{i-1} dξ_1 and the multiplicativity ξ_i ξ_j = C(i+j, i) ξ_{i+j}. The page is a sketch, not a completed classification.
errors: The list of conditions on the ξ_i is left blank. Missing are the multiplicativity relation ξ_i ξ_j = C(i+j,i) ξ_{i+j} and the d-compatibility dξ_i = ξ_{i-1} dξ_1, which are needed for φ_1 to be a differential ring map. Without them the 'canonical bijection' is not fully stated.

As written, A_i = A_1^{(i)} is imposed for every φ_1. That presumes compatibility with divided powers in degree 0 (or follows from multiplicativity only up to the factor i!), so the hypotheses are slightly conflated with the PD-compatibility criterion given in the last line.
c_{ij} is not defined. If it is the binomial coefficient, the condition is the standard divided-power-sequence condition; fine.

ideas.what: Bialgebra endomorphisms of a polynomial/divided-power Hopf algebra described by sequences τ_i with τ_iτ_j = c_{ij}τ_{i+j}
ideas.modern_name: divided-power sequences / Cartier duality between k[T] and Γ(T) (points of Ĝ_a)

ideas.what: Classification of augmented differential-algebra maps between one-variable PD de Rham complexes, allowing degree-mixing maps X ↦ A + B dX
ideas.modern_name: morphisms of PD-dg algebras / super-algebra maps of functions on odd tangent bundle ΠT (super-diffeomorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot (PD de Rham complex, 1974); supergeometry folklore (Kontsevich, Manin) for the non-graded viewpoint

ideas.what: Endomorphism of a 'Witt-type' complete differential PD bialgebra studied via a tower of semilinear invariants φ_0, φ_1, ...
ideas.modern_name: close to the structure of the de Rham-Witt complex / Frobenius-type endomorphisms of PD de Rham complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a classification of endomorphisms of a complete differential PD (Witt-type) bialgebra by successive invariants φ_0, φ_1, ... He completes only the one-variable step, and the conditions on the ξ_i are left blank. The program, which includes non-grading-preserving endomorphisms of PD de Rham complexes, is not pursued in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: essayons de déterminer les invariants de φ_*, endom de la bialg diff à p.d. complète Witt
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Non-graded (degree-mixing) automorphisms of PD de Rham / de Rham-Witt complexes appear implicitly in derived/prismatic contexts. The explicit 'super' description of such maps in the PD setting is a minor but tidy point. It is unlikely to be new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine but deliberate computation. It classifies augmented differential PD-algebra maps in one variable, including degree-mixing ones (the super viewpoint), within an unclear 'Witt bialgebra' program. It is of mild historical interest as a 1975-76 trace of de Rham-Witt-adjacent thinking, but there is no substantive unrecorded result.
transcription_corrections: The sheet is the verso of a typed SGA 7 Exp. IX page; the faint typed text showing through belongs to that typescript, not to this note.
'A_i = A_1^{(i)}' should be read with divided powers: A_i = A_1^{[i]}.
'satisfaisant à les ξ_i qui[?]' is better read as 'satisfaisant à : [conditions left blank]'; the phrase 'les ξ_i qui...' is a separate, unfinished insertion.
In the line 'Il doit être compatible avec la augm et' the reading is likely 'avec les augm. et' followed by an unfinished phrase; the struck-through text reads roughly '(compat. aux gradations ...)'.
The final line reads: 'φ est compatible avec les gradations (resp. compat. aux p.d.) ssi B_i = 0 ∀ i ≥ 1 (resp. B_i = A_1^{(i-1)} B_1 ∀ i ≥ 2).'
